digestNormalization.rationale: contractDigest is self-referential; planRevision is bound by the canonical decision
digestNormalization.stalenessRule: digest mismatch against the latest non-superseded adoption decision for this contract path is REJECT-STALE

adoptionSource: Operator chat 2026-11-12: phase request 'update the use of the A2UI to the new version 1.0 release and include all other updates to AG-UI, etc.'; /kbd-assess instruction to make the library 'a world class implementation for agentic application development'; 'Adopt all' for assessment decisions D1-D8; 'Run /kbd-plan'.
amendmentPolicy: Material scope or acceptance changes need explicit operator adoption recorded as a new canonical decision with supersedes (signed amend-contract manifest once bound). Suggestions never enter task totals on their own.

releaseClaim.userOperation: An application developer connects a conformant A2UI 1.0 agent, over AG-UI or A2A, to @prometheus-ags/a2ui-react; its surfaces render, bind to graph entities and send policy-authorized actions back, and an AG-UI 1.0 run stream drives the chat components with working cancellation and interrupt approvals, with no translation layer of the developer's own.
supportedEnvironments: React 19 in Chromium (browser flows on built examples and the packed package)
Node 22, 24 and 26 for the headless runtime and packed-consumer checks (the root engines range)
releaseClaim.currentCapabilities: At adoption: A2UI v0.9/v0.9.1 rendering through @a2ui/web_core 0.12.0; an RC-dialect 'v1.0' bridge that rejects A2UI 1.0 final; A2A on a private v0.9.1 extension URI; chat components on a bespoke event set with a no-op abort; verify:a2ui-bridge and verify:package-contracts red on #75; workspace dependencies not installed, so build health is UNKNOWN.
explicitUnknowns: Whether @a2ui/react 0.15.0 renders every 1.0 basic-catalog case through our wrapper
Final wire shape of AG-UI interrupt outcomes (marked Draft upstream)
Release timing of A2UI spec PR #4044 (@-prefixed keys) in an npm build

scenarioMatrix.name: Conformant A2UI 1.0 surface renders through the built package
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: pnpm run verify:a2ui-v1 (scripts/verify-a2ui-v1.mjs) loading the built @prometheus-ags/a2ui-react in Chromium
scenarioMatrix.oracle: createSurface, updateComponents, updateDataModel and deleteSurface with version "1.0" and @path/@call bindings render the expected DOM and data, and deleteSurface removes it
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: the same surface sent with version "v1.0" (RC) is refused with error code unsupported-protocol-version and renders nothing while the RC shim is off
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: 1.0 envelopes under a scratch fixture dir, content-digested; scratch port per run
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, DOM snapshot digest, refusal message for the negative control

scenarioMatrix.name: Real AG-UI A2UI middleware surface renders and recovery resyncs
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: pnpm run verify:a2ui-v1 driving a real @ag-ui/a2ui-middleware stream into the built runtime
scenarioMatrix.oracle: the middleware a2ui-surface activity renders a DOM identical (digest) to the same operations fed directly to the runtime; an a2ui-surface lifecycle activity with content.status "failed" (as @ag-ui/a2ui-middleware sends) produces exactly one producer-failed resync request, also when redelivered
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: an activity of an unknown type, and a lifecycle activity with status "building", cause no render and no resync
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: middleware run with a recorded scripted agent, scratch port
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, captured activity stream digest, resync request log

scenarioMatrix.name: Upstream adapter and accessibility conformance cases pass
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: pnpm run verify:a2ui-conformance against the built @prometheus-ags/a2ui-react in Chromium
realCollaborators: upstream a2ui conformance suite at a pinned commit
scenarioMatrix.oracle: every case in core/adapter_conformance.yaml and core/accessibility.yaml at the commit recorded by a2ui-v1-conformance-harness#1 (SHA and per-file digests bound into the receipt) passes, except cases in the digest-bound divergence list tests/conformance/a2ui/divergences.json; each entry names its case id, a reason class (security-policy, upstream-renderer-gap in the bundled @a2ui 0.15.0 renderer, or not-observable-through-public-API) and the step and assertion of each failure it allows; a listed case passes, or fails only on those allowances
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: a deliberately mutated copy of one case (expected output altered) fails the harness; a divergence entry whose case fails on an assertion its entry does not allow, or names no loaded case, fails the run
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: vendored suite with commit SHA and per-file SHA-256; divergences.json with its SHA-256
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, per-case results, pinned commit and digests

scenarioMatrix.name: Catalog pairing by protocol version
scenarioMatrix.oracle: a 1.0 surface resolves component catalogId, then surface catalogId, against the 1.0 catalog and renders
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: a 1.0 createSurface naming the v0.9.1 catalog id is refused with the catalog-mismatch error code recorded in design.md by a2ui-v1-native-surfaces#2
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, error code observed

scenarioMatrix.name: Bare and @-prefixed envelope keys
scenarioMatrix.oracle: a component using @catalogId/@accessibility and one using bare keys both render identically
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: a component carrying both catalogId and @catalogId is rejected
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, both DOM digests, rejection message

scenarioMatrix.name: Agent-to-renderer function calls are restricted
scenarioMatrix.oracle: callRendererFunction for an agent-callable function yields a rendererFunctionResponse with the result
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: callRendererFunction for a renderer-only function yields error code INVALID_FUNCTION_CALL and does not execute
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: catalog with one agent-callable and one renderer-only function
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, response and error payloads

scenarioMatrix.name: Renderer-to-agent function responses under policy and limits
scenarioMatrix.oracle: runtime.callAgentFunction(..., { writeTo }) answered by an agentFunctionResponse writes the value into the data model and the surface updates
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: a policy-denied action executes nothing, and an answer whose write would exceed maxDataModelBytes is not written and is reported as a limit-exceeded producer fault
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: scratch surface with policy allowing one function
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, data-model digest, denial and limit errors

scenarioMatrix.name: User-activation functions require a gesture
scenarioMatrix.oracle: the function runs after a real click
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: the same function invoked programmatically without user activation (the official resolveAction with userActivation false, the path agent-driven invocation takes) is refused and has no effect
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: scratch page with one activation-gated function
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, effect log for both runs

scenarioMatrix.name: A2A on the official A2UI v1.0 extension
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: after pnpm run build:packages: node scripts/verify-a2a-conformance.mjs --report <boundary folder>/a2a-conformance.json (packed entity-graph-a2a and the packed a2ui-react headless entry)
scenarioMatrix.oracle: a turn whose message.metadata.a2uiRendererCapabilities offers A2UI 1.0 receives DataParts (metadata.mimeType application/a2ui+json) whose data is a list of A2UI 1.0 messages that build the expected surface in the packed headless runtime; a client A2UI action DataPart is handled by the agent's a2uiInbound handler after authorize and answered
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: the same request without a2uiRendererCapabilities receives no A2UI parts (the official extension's per-turn rule; extension activation alone does not offer A2UI), and an inbound action that authorize refuses is not handled and the task is rejected
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: reference agent on a scratch port

scenarioMatrix.name: AG-UI 1.0 run stream drives EntityChat through the graph
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: pnpm run verify:agui-run-stack in Chromium against the built packages
scenarioMatrix.oracle: RUN_STARTED, TEXT_MESSAGE_*, TOOL_CALL_*, TOOL_CALL_RESULT, REASONING_* and RUN_FINISHED render in EntityChat, and the messages appear in a second view reading the graph
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: a second view mounted on a different conversation id shows none of those messages
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: scripted AG-UI agent served over SSE on a scratch port
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, graph snapshot digest, DOM digests of both views

scenarioMatrix.name: Cancellation stops superseded streams
scenarioMatrix.oracle: after a second send, the first stream's later events cause zero graph writes and the AbortSignal passed to streamFactory is aborted
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: an un-superseded stream run alongside keeps writing (proves the counter observes writes)
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, graph write counts per stream; the pre-fix defect is cited from the HEAD source in design.md (context, not evidence; no executed pre-fix reproduction was recorded)

scenarioMatrix.name: Interrupt approvals through the entity action policy
scenarioMatrix.oracle: an interrupt run outcome (shape as typed by the installed @ag-ui/core 1.0.4, mapped in design.md by agui-1-0-floors-and-middleware-interop#2) shows EntityInterruptApproval; approve and edit-before-approve resume the run with resume[] carrying the decision, and the policy audit records it
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: deny resumes with a denial and the guarded entity is unchanged; an action on a disallowed entity is refused by policy
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, resume payloads, audit records, entity digests

scenarioMatrix.name: Headless export by protocol version
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: pnpm run verify:a2ui-v1 (Node lane importing the packed ./headless entry)
realCollaborators: Node 22 or later (the boundary preamble accepts 22, 24 or 26)
scenarioMatrix.oracle: a 1.0 surface exports without theme, rebuilds in a fresh runtime, and re-exports byte-identically
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: a v0.9.1 surface with theme keeps theme through the same round trip

scenarioMatrix.name: Examples run A2UI 1.0 end to end
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: pnpm run verify:a2ui-examples (builds each example, serves the build, drives it in Chromium)
scenarioMatrix.oracle: each example, built and served, renders its main surface and completes one action in Chromium, and every A2UI envelope captured from its running producer (activity stream or producer module output, since two examples produce in the browser) has version "1.0"
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: the same envelope assertion run against each example's pre-migration envelope stream, recorded as a digested fixture by its migration task before the change, fails on its v0.9.1 or "v1.0" envelopes
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: built example outputs, scratch ports, pre-migration envelope recordings with digests
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, screenshots in the dated evidence folder

scenarioMatrix.name: Packed consumers type-check strictly and the zod advisory stays closed
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: pnpm run verify:a2ui-bridge && pnpm run verify:package-contracts
scenarioMatrix.oracle: both scripts exit 0 with skipLibCheck false in every packed consumer, which install the registry (unpatched) @a2ui/* if they install it at all, and the bundled a2ui-react runtime resolves its zod imports to zod 4.6.7 via zod/v3
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: a control consumer in the same run that imports @a2ui/web_core/v0_9 directly from the registry with skipLibCheck false fails with TS2835, proving the check would catch the upstream declaration
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: packed tarballs in scratch consumer dirs
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit codes, consumer reports, resolved zod version

scenarioMatrix.name: Exports, skills, release contract and generated docs in sync
scenarioMatrix.productionEntry: pnpm run verify:skills && pnpm run validate && pnpm run docs:artifacts:check
scenarioMatrix.oracle: all three commands exit 0 after refresh:exports and a fresh build
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: the scratch-copy control authored by a2ui-1-0-release-sync#1, run as part of verify:skills in the boundary: removing one export from packages/a2ui-react/src/index.ts and rebuilding without refresh:exports makes verify:skills fail
scenarioMatrix.classification: delivery-only; its failure is never reported as a product failure

scenarioMatrix.name: RC-input shim is opt-in and maps RC actions to 1.0 function calls
scenarioMatrix.oracle: with acceptReleaseCandidateInput, an RC "v1.0" envelope renders the same DOM as its 1.0 equivalent, and an RC wantResponse action is sent as a callAgentFunction whose agentFunctionResponse (or RC actionResponse with the same id) is written at the former responsePath
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: with the shim at its default (off), the same RC envelope is refused (shared with UPG-1)

scenarioMatrix.name: Flutter showcase renders A2UI 1.0 final through a2ui_flutter under the Riverpod action policy
scenarioMatrix.oracle: the integration test on the simulator renders the task-board surface from version "1.0" messages, a policy-approved user action yields a receipt and the graph change, and the pubspec resolves a2ui_flutter 0.3.0 with no genui dependency
scenarioMatrix.negativeControl: a surface naming an unknown component or catalog renders nothing, writes nothing to the graph and shows the refusal; a denied action produces a denial receipt and no graph change
scenarioMatrix.fixtures: the showcase's own surface messages, content-digested
scenarioMatrix.evidence: argv, exit code, flutter test output, resolved package versions

resilienceScope.policy: Cancellation (UPG-11), the function and user-activation refusals (UPG-6, UPG-8), policy denial and limit rejection (UPG-7, UPG-12), and the zod advisory (UPG-15) never defer via budget overflow; exhaustion means checkpoint and BLOCKED.
deferredOptional: Load testing with many concurrent surfaces
Progressive rendering beyond what the conformance suite requires (W11)

exclusions: W8 devtools inspector, W9 OpenTelemetry, W10 beyond conformance-required accessibility, W11, W12 MCP Apps (D4)
Shipping W5 attested approvals or W6 graph-bound UI (design only, change 8)

Tagging or merging without a separate operator approval; publishing to npm or pub.dev before the boundary run and isolated review pass, or without the operator confirming the versions and the npm dist-tag; publishing the Rust crates to crates.io
AG-UI SUBAGENT_* events and multimodal message parts (no adopted scenario needs them)
AUI-16/AUI-18 discrimination check and npm provenance carried from phase-v4-a2ui-runtime-hardening (release-process debt)
The PLAUSIBLE stale-history read in use-chat-session (unobserved; raised as a question, not tasked)
requiredSafetyChecks: Catalog and component allow-listing unchanged or stronger for both protocol versions
Action policy and entity-graph policy decide every executed action, including interrupt approvals
Resource limits applied to every new message type and to function responses
zod advisory GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 not reopened in the bundled runtime
No secrets or user data in logs or evidence

budgets.exhaustion: checkpoint and BLOCKED; never a silent PASS; docs and state may be saved without running product checks
